title: Quantifying the diagnostic time gap in precision oncology: A retrospective analysis of potential time savings from same-day cartridge-based molecular testing versus next-generation sequencing in cytology specimens.
authors: Tran K, Chen E, Symmans WF et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Next-generation sequencing (NGS) turnaround times (TAT) exceed two weeks and can delay the initiation of targeted therapy. Rapid cartridge-based platforms such as Idylla deliver single-gene or fusion results from minimal cytology material within hours, but time savings have not been systematically quantified.
METHODS: Forty-two cases of non-small cell lung carcinoma, thyroid carcinoma, melanoma, and mammary analogue secretory carcinoma of the salivary gland that underwent both Idylla testing (KRAS, EGFR, BRAF, and GeneFusion assays) and orthogonal NGS at a single academic center were reviewed. NGS TAT was calculated from specimen collection to report release, and Idylla results were modeled as available one day after collection. The primary outcome was per-case time savings (NGS TAT minus one day); treatment timelines were reconstructed from the medical record. Analyses were descriptive; no inferential testing was performed. A sensitivity analysis varied the modeled Idylla TAT from 1 to 3 days, and an adjusted estimate assigned no time saving to the two cartridge results that were not actionable on the day of collection.
RESULTS: The median NGS TAT across all 42 cases was 20.0 days (IQR, 17.0-23.8; range, 8-51). Against the modeled 1-day Idylla TAT, the median time savings was 19.0 days per case (IQR, 16.0-22.8; range, 7-50), totaling 858 patient-days. Assigning no time saving to those two cases gave a median of 18.0 days and 817 patient-days. No patient received therapy that was subsequently contradicted by the sequencing result. In thirteen patients, the sequencing interval alone exceeded three weeks, and in seven, no systemic therapy was underway while the result was awaited.
CONCLUSIONS: Same-day cartridge-based testing from cytology and small biopsy specimens could provide actionable results a median of 19 days earlier than standard NGS. Whether this translates into earlier treatment initiation was not assessed and requires prospective evaluation.

title: Genetic signatures of lung cancer: association and biomarker potential of EGFR, KRAS, and HER2 polymorphisms.
authors: Ortiz TC, Qasim N, Bashir K et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Lung cancer is a key global health challenge. Genetic variations in the key oncogenic pathways, including EGFR, HER2, and KRAS, can contribute to personal susceptibility and disease progression. The objective of this study was to assess the association between single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in candidate genes, including KRAS, HER2, and EGFR, and lung cancer risk in the Pakistani population.
METHODOLOGY: The case-control study comprised 600 participants, including 300 patients with histologically verified lung cancer and 300 healthy controls. DNA was extracted, followed by ARMS-PCR for genotyping.
RESULTS: Genetic research revealed a strong correlation between EGFR (rs712829) and lung cancer risk. The mutant (TT) genotype had a protective effect (OR = 0.11; 95% CI = 0.07-0.17; p < 0.0001), whereas the mutant (GT) significantly increased the risk (OR = 3.27; 95%CI = 2.32-4.60; p < 0.0001). The polymorphisms of the other two genes, HER2 and KRAS, did not show any significant association with disease. All demographic parameters, including age, gender, and smoking, did not show any significant association in our studied population.
CONCLUSIONS: This study determined that polymorphisms in the EGFR and KRAS genes were found to be significantly associated with lung cancer risk, whereas HER2 variations were found to have a potential protective role.

title: Small-Molecule Drugs Approved by the FDA in 2025.
authors: Wang X, Wang Y, Luo R et al.
abstract: In today's pharmaceutical sector, innovation is not only the core driver of industry upgrading, but also closely tied to patient health and well-being. A drug's innovative mechanism of action, physiological effects, chemical structure, and indications collectively reflect both its clinical therapeutic value and the novelty of underlying basic research. This article presents the innovative advances of 31 small-molecule drugs (accounting for 67.4%) approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in 2025. These therapeutics span multiple therapeutic areas, including oncology, autoimmune diseases, infectious diseases, cardiovascular disorders, and metabolic conditions, and target a diverse array of molecular targets such as mitogen-activated protein kinase kinases 1 and 2 (MEK1/2), colony-stimulating factor 1 receptor, protein tyrosine kinase Tec, and Bruton tyrosine kinase, among others. Among these approved small-molecule drugs, 13 are designated as "first-in-class" therapies, reflecting the continuous innovation in the field of new drug development. Notably, many of these drugs (e.g., Journavx, Brinsupri, Jascayd, and Kygevvi) have also been granted breakthrough therapy designation, which underscores that they not only feature novel mechanisms of action, but also deliver clinically meaningful efficacy advantages over prior therapeutic options. Notably, in 2025, the FDA approved sunvozertinib, a novel small-molecule drug independently developed by Dizal (Jiangsu, China) Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., for locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) exon 20 insertion mutations, contributing Chinese wisdom and solutions to the transformative evolution of global drug development paradigms. Cross-technology integration, long-acting drug delivery, and precision medicine stand as core industrial trends, enabling innovative drugs to boost therapeutic efficacy, mitigate toxic side effects and refine patients' medical experience, offering patients expanded regimens for improved survival outcomes. With the development of first-in-class drugs, therapies targeting previously undruggable targets-or those inaccessible via conventional approaches-are entering clinical practice, creating major opportunities for novel, mechanism-based drug discovery. This article comprehensively analyzes the mechanisms of action, synthesis methods, and clinical trials of these drugs chronologically, and delineates emerging trends in novel drug development.

title: Novel 2,4-Pyrimidinediamine Derivative as Potent EGFR Inhibitor for NSCLC Treatment.
authors: Jia S, Lv X, Lv J et al.
abstract: Aberrant activation of EGFR drives the progression of non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). As one of the most prevalent driver genes in NSCLC, EGFR represents a critical therapeutic target for patients with NSCLC. In this study, we synthesized 2,4-pyrimidinediamine derivative ZX-3. Compared to its lead compound ceritinib, which has weak cytotoxicity for EGFR-driven NSCLC, ZX-3 exhibited potent cytotoxicity against EGFR-driven NSCLC. We further investigated the antitumor activity and mechanisms of ZX-3 both in vitro and in vivo. Through high-throughput target screening using RTK protein arrays and surface plasmon resonance (SPR) assays, it was demonstrated that ZX-3 reversibly targets the EGFR protein and inhibits its downstream PI3K/AKT signaling pathway. In vitro experiments revealed that ZX-3 suppresses cell colony formation in H2228 cells, induces G1-phase cell cycle arrest, and promotes apoptosis. In in vivo xenograft studies, ZX-3 treatment significantly suppressed tumor growth without obvious toxicity. Collectively, ZX-3 represents a reversible EGFR inhibitor based on borylation modification and possesses favorable antitumor activity both in vitro and in vivo, offering a novel strategy for the subsequent development of EGFR-targeted inhibitors.

title: Design, Synthesis, In Vitro and In Silico Evaluation of Triazole-Benzimidazole Hybrid Derivatives as Potential Inhibitors of EGFR, EGFR-L858R, and EGFR-L858R/T790M.
authors: Uslu H, Hıdır A, Yumuşak E et al.
abstract: Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) has become one of the most important molecular targets for the development of anticancer agents because of its critical role in regulating cell proliferation, differentiation, and survival. In the present study, a novel series of benzimidazole-triazole derivatives were designed by incorporating pharmacophoric features of clinically used EGFR inhibitors, synthesized, characterized, and evaluated for their anticancer potential. Cytotoxicity studies against the A549 lung cancer cell line identified 2-((4-Ethyl-5-(2-(4-hydroxyphenyl)-1H-benzo[d]imidazol-6-yl)-4H-1,2,4-triazol-3-yl)thio)-N-methylacetamide, 2-((4-Ethyl-5-(2-(4-hydroxyphenyl)-1H-benzo[d]imidazol-6-yl)-4H-1,2,4-triazol-3-yl)thio)-N-(hydroxymethyl)acetamide, 2-((4-Ethyl-5-(2-(4-hydroxyphenyl)-1H-benzo[d]imidazol-6-yl)-4H-1,2,4-triazol-3-yl)thio)-N-methoxy-N-methylacetamide, and 2-((4-Ethyl-5-(2-(4-hydroxyphenyl)-1H-benzo[d]imidazol-6-yl)-4H-1,2,4-triazol-3-yl)thio)-N-phenylacetamide as active derivatives, with compound 5a exhibiting the highest antiproliferative activity (IC50 = 6.014 ± 0.758 µM), and relatively low cytotoxicity toward NIH/3T3 cells. Based on these findings, 2-((4-Ethyl-5-(2-(4-hydroxyphenyl)-1H-benzo[d]imidazol-6-yl)-4H-1,2,4-triazol-3-yl)thio)-N-methylacetamide was further evaluated against EGFR and its clinically relevant mutant forms, EGFR-L858R and EGFR-L858R/T790M. Retrospective in silico ADME analysis indicated that the synthesized compounds generally possessed favorable drug-like properties, with 2-((4-Ethyl-5-(2-(4-hydroxyphenyl)-1H-benzo[d]imidazol-6-yl)-4H-1,2,4-triazol-3-yl)thio)-N-methylacetamide showing the most favorable overall drug-likeness profile among the series. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics studies revealed that compound 2-((4-Ethyl-5-(2-(4-hydroxyphenyl)-1H-benzo[d]imidazol-6-yl)-4H-1,2,4-triazol-3-yl)thio)-N-methylacetamide formed stable interactions with key residues in the ATP-binding site of unmutated EGFR, supporting the in vitro inhibition results. Overall, synthesized benzimidazole-triazole derivatives may be promising precursor compounds for the development of novel EGFR inhibitors, particularly against unmutated EGFR cancer cells.

title: AI-Driven Multi-Omics Approaches for Deciphering Small-Cell Lung Cancer Heterogeneity Using Nucleic-Acid-Based Features.
authors: Zeeshan S, McVey C, Majeed S et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) is a rare but highly aggressive malignancy defined by rapid progression, early metastasis, and profound therapeutic resistance. Its extensive heterogeneity across genomic, transcriptomic, epigenetic, proteomic, and microenvironmental levels continues to undermine precision medicine. Emerging evidence highlights the complex role of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) alterations, histologic transformation from EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) to SCLC, and the influence of distinct transcriptional subtypes on clinical behavior.
METHODS: This review synthesizes current literature encompassing nucleic-acid-based determinants of resistance, SCLC molecular architecture, transformation biology, and subtype evolution, integrating findings from genomic, transcriptomic, epigenetic, proteomic, imaging, and clinical studies. We additionally evaluated artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) methodologies with potential to unify multi-omics, radiomics, and clinical variables to model subtype plasticity, clonal evolution, and therapy-induced rewiring.
RESULTS: The evidence demonstrates that traditional single-layer analyses are insufficient to capture the multiscale architecture of SCLC biology or the nonlinear interactions driving resistance, whereas AI-enabled multi-omics approaches offer advantages in enhancing subtype classification, supporting early detection, and improving prediction of therapeutic response. Key barriers such as tissue scarcity, limited biomarker availability, and extreme intratumoral heterogeneity remain significant challenges, though increasingly addressable through integrative computational frameworks.
CONCLUSION: AI-driven systems-level integration reframes SCLC as a dynamically evolving, multilayered disease process, where nucleic-acid alterations are central to subtype evolution and treatment resistance, providing a conceptual model to guide biomarker discovery and therapeutic development. By leveraging AI-enabled multi-omics and radiomics, this framework has the potential to advance personalized clinical management and overcome longstanding diagnostic and therapeutic challenges in SCLC.

title: Longitudinal Assessment of EGFR and MET Transcriptional Activity Using Cell-Free Chromatin Immunoprecipitation in Two Patients with EGFR-Mutated Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
authors: Pedersen E, Maansson CT, Meldgaard P et al.
abstract: Background/Objectives:MET amplification represents the most common bypass resistance mechanism to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) treatment in EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Combination therapy with the EGFR-TKI, osimertinib, and the MET-TKI, crizotinib, has demonstrated clinical efficacy in overcoming this resistance. However, assessing MET transcriptional activity during treatment remains challenging. Methods: Cell-free chromatin immunoprecipitation (cfChIP) targeting H3 lysine 36 trimethylation (H3K36me3) was employed to investigate the transcriptional activity of the EGFR and MET genes in serial liquid biopsies obtained from two patients with EGFR-mutated NSCLC. Droplet digital PCR (ddPCR) was used to quantify circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) and cfChIP enrichment levels. Results: In PT1, H3K36me3 mEGFR and MET cfChIP enrichment increased during disease progression, with MET enrichment increasing further following the initiation of crizotinib/osimertinib combination therapy, during which the patient experienced a partial response. In PT2, MET amplification was detected in a liquid biopsy, but MET cfChIP enrichment remained low throughout the treatment course, and the patient did not respond to crizotinib. Conclusions: This two-patient feasibility study illustrates the potential of cfChIP-ddPCR for the longitudinal assessment of EGFR and MET transcriptional activity in liquid biopsies. These observations warrant further investigation of cfChIP as an approach for monitoring transcriptional activity during osimertinib/crizotinib treatment.

title: Biomarker Integration in the Perioperative Management of Early-Stage Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer.
authors: Rabinovich EP, Martin LW
abstract: The concept of personalized medicine has tremendous appeal-tailoring diagnosis and treatment to an individual, rather than a "one-size-fits-all" approach. The management of non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) has rapidly evolved toward strategies increasingly guided by tumor biology and precision oncology. The safety and significant efficacy of biomarker-directed therapies in metastatic disease have fueled interest in applying precision oncology to early-stage, operable NSCLC. Advances in molecular profiling have revealed that a substantial proportion of resected NSCLC harbor actionable driver mutations, enabling the integration of targeted therapies into the perioperative setting. The success of adjuvant epidermal growth factor receptor and anaplastic lymphoma kinase inhibition established a framework for biomarker-driven therapy and highlights the importance of comprehensive molecular testing at diagnosis. In parallel, perioperative immune checkpoint inhibitor-based strategies have expanded treatment options for appropriately selected patients, further emphasizing the importance of molecular profiling. Significant implementation gaps remain, including incomplete molecular testing, delayed results, inadequate tissue sampling, fragmented workflows, and disparities in access. Beyond clinically actionable driver mutations, emerging research highlights radiogenomics and advances in the use of circulating tumor DNA for minimal residual disease detection, with important implications for early recurrence detection and patient prognostication, although these technologies differ in clinical maturity. Collectively, these developments emphasize the molecular heterogeneity underlying early-stage NSCLC and the expanding role of biomarkers in guiding clinical decision-making. Integrating genomic, radiographic, and biologic markers into clinical workflows will be essential to refine risk stratification, personalize perioperative treatment strategies, and ultimately improve long-term oncologic outcomes.

title: Firmonertinib Plus Chemotherapy for Unresectable EGFR PACC-Mutant Stage III Lung Cancer: A Phase II Study
conditions: EGFR Positive Non-small Cell Lung Cancer
summary: This is a prospective, single-arm, multicenter Phase II clinical study. It aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of Firmonertinib combined with chemotherapy in patients with unresectable Stage III lung adenocarcinoma harboring EGFR PACC mutations. Participants will receive Firmonertinib combined with standard chemotherapy. The primary objective is to assess the objective response rate (ORR). This study will provide important evidence for a potential new treatment option for this specific patient population.

title: [Non-small cell lung cancer: a comparative analysis of methods for assessing TROP2 expression in relation to clinical and morphological characteristics].
authors: Vtorushin SV, Loos DM, Tashireva LA et al.
abstract:
UNLABELLED: Trophoblast cell surface antigen 2 (TROP2) has emerged as a promising therapeutic target in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in the context of the development of antibody-drug conjugates. In this setting, reproducible and biologically meaningful immunohistochemical assessment of TROP2 expression, taking into account its intracellular localization, is of particular importance.
OBJECTIVE: To characterize TROP2 expression in lung adenocarcinomas and squamous cell carcinomas and to evaluate its association with clinicopathological parameters using different immunohistochemical assessment methods.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 60 cases of NSCLC (30 adenocarcinomas and 30 squamous cell carcinomas) diagnosed between 2019 and 2023. TROP2 expression was evaluated by immunohistochemistry using the semi-quantitative H-score and the normalized membrane ratio (NMR), reflecting the relative contribution of membranous and cytoplasmic expression. Associations between TROP2 expression and clinicopathological characteristics were analyzed.
RESULTS: TROP2 expression was detected in all examined NSCLC samples. TROP2 expression assessed by H-score was significantly higher in squamous cell carcinoma compared with lung adenocarcinoma (p=0.0001), whereas NMR values did not differ between histological subtypes. No associations were observed between H-score and clinicopathological parameters. In contrast, NMR demonstrated histotype-dependent associations: with tumor stage in lung adenocarcinoma (p=0.0483) and with lymphovascular invasion in squamous cell carcinoma (p=0.0139). The proportion of cases meeting the NMR-based criteria for TROP2 positivity was low.
CONCLUSION: The results indicate that the choice of TROP2 assessment method substantially influences data interpretation. Consideration of intracellular protein localization using the NMR appears to be more informative than conventional semi-quantitative approaches and may reflect biological features of tumor progression in NSCLC.

title: Cost-Effectiveness of Telisotuzumab Vedotin-tllv for Previously Treated High c-Met Protein-Overexpressing Nonsquamous Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer in the United States.
authors: Weiss GJ
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To estimate the incremental cost-effectiveness of telisotuzumab vedotin-tllv (teliso-V) versus docetaxel in previously treated high c-Met protein-overexpressing (≥50% of tumor cells with 3+ staining) advanced nonsquamous non-small cell lung cancer.
METHODS: A partitioned survival model with monthly cycles and a five-year horizon was built from the US healthcare sector perspective. Individual time-to-event data were reconstructed from published Kaplan-Meier curves of the c-Met High subgroup (N=78) of LUMINOSITY and the CONTACT-01 docetaxel arm (N=180). Because individual covariate data were unavailable, a naive (unadjusted) indirect comparison was conducted. Seven parametric distributions were fit independently by arm; their median and range were the primary summary. The analysis was preregistered.
RESULTS: The unadjusted overall survival hazard ratio favored teliso-V but was not statistically significant (HR 0.690; 95% CI 0.471-1.010). The median incremental cost-effectiveness ratio was approximately $2.0 million per QALY (range, $1.7-$2.2 million). Across 70,000 probabilistic iterations, cost-effectiveness was not achieved in any iteration at $50,000, $100,000, $150,000, or $200,000 per QALY. The threshold payment limit at $150,000 per QALY was approximately $1,209 per 100 mg (92% reduction).
CONCLUSIONS: At the current Medicare Part B payment limit, telisotuzumab vedotin-tllv is unlikely to be cost-effective versus docetaxel in the US high c-Met protein-overexpressing population at conventional willingness-to-pay thresholds. The conclusion was robust to modeled survival extrapolation and parameter uncertainty. Because the comparison is unadjusted, comparative effectiveness remains uncertain pending randomized results.

title: Metastasis Extraction From Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer Clinical Notes Using Large Language Model-Based Classification: Retrospective Comparative Study.
authors: Balaji S, Campbell K, Chen RZ et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Identification of metastasis status in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is a critical part of understanding disease prognosis, treatment courses, trial eligibility, and population-level cancer surveillance. However, metastasis status is inconsistently recorded in structured cancer registry fields, since manual abstraction of clinical notes is often an error-prone process. This challenge highlights an opportunity for leveraging large language models (LLMs) to conduct high-scale metastasis extraction from real-world clinical documentation.
OBJECTIVE: We conducted a retrospective, multicohort comparative evaluation of 3 distinct LLMs for 2 independent classification tasks: overall metastasis presence at any site and brain/central nervous system (CNS) metastasis presence. We evaluated model performance on 2 independent NSCLC cohorts: one with registry labels and another with manual annotations. We further explored whether our methods could analyze clinical documentation and recover missing information in structured registry fields.
METHODS: Patient cohorts were derived from the Winship Cancer Institute. Cohort 1 (n=579 patients; 24,887 notes across 69 note types; 2023-2025) used registry-linked metastasis fields as the reference standard. Cohort 2 (n=22 patients; 644 radiology notes; 2010-2021) was drawn from 2 completed randomized trials and used dual-annotated labels (Cohen κ: 0.93 overall metastasis; 0.88 CNS metastasis) as the reference standard. We fine-tuned the GatorTron-base encoder model for each independent binary classification task. We evaluated MedGemma-27B-text and Llama 3.1-70B using zero-shot prompting. A separate cohort of 675 patients with missing registry labels was used for an exploratory missingness-recovery analysis, validated against annotations of a random subsample. Our best-performing model was used to conduct further site-specific metastasis classification, based on available registry data.
RESULTS: More than half (675/1260, 54%) of initially identified cohort 1 patients had missing or unknown registry metastasis labels. MedGemma demonstrated the best performance in overall metastasis classification (cohort 1: F1-score=0.80; cohort 2 patient-level: F1-score=1.0; cohort 2 note-level: F1-score=0.93). For brain/CNS metastasis, Llama3 performed best in both cohorts (cohort 1: F1-score=0.79; cohort 2 patient-level: F1-score=0.93; cohort 2 note-level: F1-score=0.86). The fine-tuned GatorTron model showed strong performance for classification of overall metastasis in cohort 1 (F1-score=0.72). Error analysis indicated that several model errors reflected incomplete registry labels, ambiguous clinical language, or missing documentation. In the exploratory recovery analysis, model predictions agreed with manual annotations at an accuracy of 0.90 and F1-score of 0.89. Additional site-specific metastasis classification by MedGemma demonstrated high performance for liver metastasis (F1-score=0.82) and bone metastasis (F1-score=0.79).
CONCLUSIONS: All models demonstrated relatively high performance. The zero-shot generative models were more robust to nuanced documentation and context-dependent brain/CNS metastasis extraction. The fine-tuned encoder model demonstrated strong classification performance but may have been limited by potential inaccuracies in the registry reference standards during model training. This study further demonstrated the potential of LLMs in recovering plausible structured labels from narrative text, complementing cancer registries for metastasis ascertainment.

title: Multimodal Transformer Integrating CT and Pathology for Postoperative Risk Stratification in Stage I Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
authors: Wang L, Zong Y, Li X et al.
abstract: Purpose To develop and evaluate an interpretable, multimodal deep learning model to improve postoperative risk stratification and predict adjuvant therapy benefit in stage I non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Materials and Methods In this multicenter retrospective study of patients with stage I NSCLC, a multimodal model called the Deep Learning-Radiomic-Text Transformer (DLRTransformer) was developed by integrating multiview 2.5-dimensional deep learning features from CT scans, radiomics, clinical variables, and prognostic embeddings extracted from pathology reports using a large language model. A central transformer architecture fuses these features to predict disease-free survival. Model performance was evaluated on independent external datasets and compared with guideline-based risk stratification. Associations between model-derived risk scores and tumor microenvironment features were analyzed to assess biologic interpretability. Results A total of 1073 patients (mean age ± SD, 60.8 years ± 9.8; 550 male) were enrolled from five centers. On external datasets, DLRTransformer demonstrated robust prognostic performance (concordance index, 0.77-0.78), outperforming the guideline-based risk stratification (concordance index, 0.60-0.65). Risk scores were associated with tumor microenvironment phenotypes, including increased neoplastic cellularity and reduced tertiary lymphoid structures. A treatment-by-risk interaction was observed (interaction hazard ratio [HR], 0.14; 95% CI: 0.06, 0.32; P < .01). In propensity score-matched subcohorts, adjuvant therapy improved disease-free survival in high-risk patients (HR, 0.30; 95% CI: 0.11, 0.84; P = .02) but not in low-risk patients (HR, 1.70; 95% CI: 0.97, 2.99; P = .06). Conclusion The DLRTransformer improved postoperative risk stratification compared with guideline-based risk stratification and identified patients with stage I NSCLC who benefited from adjuvant therapy. Keywords: Deep Learning, Large Language Models LLMs, CT, Prognosis & Prediction, Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC), Multimodal Deep Learning, Risk Stratification, Adjuvant Therapy, Tumor Microenvironment (TME) Supplemental material is available for this article. © The Author(s) 2026. title: A Systematic Intracranial Exposure-Response Evaluation of Brain-Penetrant Inhibitors: Informing Dose Selection for Brain Metastases.
authors: Zhao Y, Huang W
abstract: Brain metastases (BMs) represent a major clinical challenge due to their high incidence in cancers such as non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and breast cancer, and the limited efficacy of systemic therapies resulting from inadequate drug penetration across the blood-brain barrier. Although several brain-penetrant tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) have been developed, the quantitative relationship between intracranial drug exposure and intracranial clinical response has not been well established, leaving an important gap in dose selection strategies. In this study, we systematically evaluated the intracranial exposure-response relationship across brain-penetrant small-molecule TKIs. Fourteen TKIs were identified based on guideline-recommended therapies for BMs. For each drug, plasma and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) pharmacokinetic profiles were simulated using published population pharmacokinetic models, with CSF exposures extrapolated using known unbound plasma fractions and CSF-to-plasma unbound concentration ratios (Kp,uu,CSF) in humans. Key intracranial exposure metrics, including the CSF steady-state trough and average concentrations relative to IC50 (Cmin,ss/IC50 and Cave,ss/IC50) and the percentage of the steady-state dosing interval during which CSF concentrations remained above IC50 (T% > IC50), were derived and correlated with intracranial outcomes from published clinical studies. Overall, significant positive correlations were observed between intracranial exposure metrics and both intracranial objective response rate (ORR) and complete response rate (CR). Greater exposure coverage above IC50 was associated with improved intracranial efficacy. This work demonstrates a positive intracranial exposure-response relationship across brain-penetrant TKIs and provides a quantitative benchmark to inform dose selection beyond traditional plasma exposure metrics. These findings highlight the importance of achieving sufficient CNS drug concentrations to optimize the therapeutic effect in patients with BMs.

title: Aberrant Myelopoiesis and Haematopoietic Stem Cell Niche Remodelling Precedes Cancer Cachexia Onset in a Sex-Dependent Manner.
authors: Tate A, Brown A, Ek Orloff L et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Male cancer patients are 30% more likely to develop cachexia compared to females; however, the underlying aetiology remains unknown. Myelopoiesis induces inflammation in cancer cachexia, which contributes to muscle atrophy. Whether differences in myelopoiesis during cancer cachexia initiation contribute to sex-based differences in cachexia incidence remains unknown.
METHODS: Male and female C57BL/6 and B6(C)-Ccr2tm1.1Cln/J mice were randomized into sham (PBS) or were inoculated subcutaneously with Lewis lung carcinoma (LLC) to induce cachexia. Mice were sacrificed 2 (14 days), 2.5 (17 days) and 3.5 weeks (24 days) post-inoculation. Changes in body composition, haematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs), myeloid immune cell migration, bone marrow niche cellular dynamics and CCL2 expression were assessed.
RESULTS: LLC inoculation reduced tumour-free body weight, lean mass, gastrocnemius-soleus mass and myofiber cross-sectional area (CSA) in males at 3.5 weeks (p < 0.05), while females maintained tumour-free body weight, lean mass and CSA. Within the bone marrow, haematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) were increased at 2, 2.5 and 3.5 weeks compared to sham in males and at 2.5 weeks compared to 2 and 3.5 weeks in females (p < 0.05). Multipotent progenitors (MPPs) were significantly increased at 2, 2.5 and 3.5 weeks compared to sham in males and at 2.5 weeks compared to sham, 2 and 3.5 weeks in females (p < 0.05). Downstream, common myeloid progenitors (CMPs) and granulocyte-monocyte progenitors (GMPs) were elevated in males at 2.5 weeks, with CCR2+GMPs peaking at 2.5 weeks in males and 3.5 weeks in females (p < 0.05). Sex differences in HSC niche composition were also observed with osteoprogenitors, osteoblasts and endothelial cells increased at 2 weeks in males, while females showed increased osteoprogenitors and endothelial progenitors at 2.5 weeks in tumour-bearing mice (p < 0.05). Plasma C-C motif chemokine ligand 2 (CCL2) concentrations increased with tumour progression in both sexes; however, CCR2+-progenitors and macrophages were decreased at 2.5 and 3.5 weeks compared to 2 weeks (p < 0.05). In skeletal muscle, CCL2 concentration increased at 3.5 weeks, and the proportion of CCR2+/CD206- macrophages increased, while total macrophage abundance remained unchanged (p < 0.05). Macrophage subpopulations were related to decreasing CSA in males but not females.
CONCLUSION: Our study suggests that aberrant myelopoiesis and sex-specific HSC niche remodelling precede muscle atrophy during cachexia development in males. These findings provide an important first step in understanding the role aberrant myelopoiesis plays in cancer cachexia and establish myeloid skewing as a potential therapeutic target.

title: Orthopaedic Management of Bone Metastases from Lung Cancer.
authors: Martins Lopes J, Oliveira V, Cardoso P et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Bone metastases from lung cancer can cause pain, pathological fracture, spinal instability, metastatic spinal cord compression and loss of independence. Lung cancer-specific evidence for orthopaedically relevant local management remains fragmented. This review assessed outcomes across spinal, appendicular and pelvic skeletal disease, while explicitly examining the anatomical distribution and limitations of the evidence.
METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, Europe PMC and Scopus were searched for original studies published from January 2015 to December 2025. Eligible studies evaluated orthopaedic, surgical, minimally invasive or percutaneous skeletal interventions, including radiotherapy when combined with or directly compared with an orthopaedically relevant local strategy. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data and completed the full Joanna Briggs Institute checklist applicable to each design. Findings were synthesised narratively, with evidence certainty assessed using GRADE.
RESULTS: Thirty-three studies comprising 3585 participants with lung cancer were included; 26 were retrospective observational studies. Thirty studies predominantly evaluated axial disease, mainly spinal metastases, whereas only six included appendicular lesions; these categories were not mutually exclusive. Local interventions were associated with pain relief, maintenance or recovery of ambulation, neurological improvement and local symptom control in selected patients. Comparative survival findings were inconsistent and vulnerable to selection bias and confounding by indication; no causal survival benefit of surgery was established. Complication patterns differed by intervention type. Overall certainty was low to very low and was weakest for appendicular and pelvic disease.
CONCLUSIONS: Orthopaedic management can be clinically important for preserving function and controlling mechanical or neurological complications, but the evidence is substantially stronger for spinal than for extraspinal disease. Treatment should remain multidisciplinary and individualised. The proposed decision frameworks are conceptual and guideline-informed rather than validated treatment algorithms.

title: From Thoracotomy to Robotic Platforms in Thoracic Surgery: Technical Evolution, Simulation-Based Training, and Surgical Outcomes.
authors: Piazzolla M, Sampietro D, Delcuratolo MD et al.
abstract: Thoracic surgery has progressively moved from open thoracotomy to video-assisted and robot-assisted approaches, reducing access-related trauma while changing the technical environment in which pulmonary resections are performed and taught. This narrative review examines the clinical evolution of open, video-assisted thoracic surgery (VATS), and robot-assisted thoracic surgery (RATS), with particular attention to the evidence supporting their perioperative and oncological outcomes, the learning curves associated with minimally invasive surgery, and the role of simulation-based training. Randomized trials now provide robust evidence that VATS improve postoperative recovery compared with thoracotomy in appropriately selected patients with predominantly early-stage non-small cell lung cancer, without compromising long-term oncological outcomes. Randomized comparisons between RATS and VATS support RATS as an oncologically acceptable minimally invasive alternative and suggest advantages in selected technical endpoints, particularly blood loss and lymph node retrieval, but do not demonstrate consistent superiority in major clinical or survival outcomes. Learning curves vary according to previous experience, case complexity, supervision, institutional volume, and the endpoint used to define competence, making fixed case-number thresholds an incomplete measure of proficiency. Simulation can improve selected technical skills and provide objective performance assessment, although evidence becomes progressively less robust when moving from simulator performance to operating room transfer and patient-level outcomes. Surgical approach, therefore, should be interpreted within a broader framework that includes patient and tumour characteristics, oncological quality, surgical expertise, institutional resources, and structured training.

title: Early and Multimodal Care for Patients with Lung Cancer: Findings from the ACCEPT Study.
authors: Grah C, Oei SL, Kindler F et al.
abstract: Objective: Treating lung cancer with a combination of targeted cancer therapy, supportive, and psychosocial treatments is important in modern oncology. The ACCEPT study investigated the efficacy of a 12-week early multimodal supportive care program on quality of life. Methods: ACCEPT was a single-center, non-randomized, prospective, open-label trial, with a pragmatic real-world design guided by patient choice. Patients with newly diagnosed, stage II-IV lung cancer participated in the outpatient ACCEPT program (psycho-oncology, health education, and training-based interventions alongside standard care). Longitudinal patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) were collected. The primary outcome was the change in quality of life at 12 weeks measured by the Trial Outcome Index (TOI). Secondary outcomes included further exploratory PROM changes and overall survival. Results: Between April 2018 and August 2021, 214 lung cancer patients (median age 67, 53% male, 57% stage IV) were enrolled, with 116 patients evaluable for longitudinal PROM changes at 12 weeks. Participation in the multimodal ACCEPT program was associated with up to 17% improvement in the TOI, psychological distress, and sleep quality (p < 0.0001). Multivariate analyses revealed that greater session attendance was significantly and dose-dependently associated with improvements in the TOI as well as reductions in depression and anxiety. Higher engagement in multimodal sessions was also linked to reduced fatigue. Furthermore, exploratory signals of improved overall survival were observed among the 40 patients (18.7%) who fully completed the ACCEPT program. Conclusions: This pragmatic, patient-centered, multimodal supportive care program for lung cancer patients was associated with dose-dependent improvements in quality of life and psychological distress. While exploratory signals of improved survival were observed, multicenter randomized controlled trials are required to confirm these findings and firmly establish the role of such supportive care programs in routine oncology.

title: Robotic-Assisted Bronchoscopy for Peripheral Pulmonary Lesions: Current Evidence, Clinical Applications, and Future Directions.
authors: Kanchustambham V
abstract: The evaluation of peripheral pulmonary lesions (PPLs) is a persistent clinical challenge, made more pressing by the expansion of low-dose CT lung cancer screening. Conventional and earlier navigational bronchoscopy, including electromagnetic navigation, historically achieved diagnostic yields of approximately 60-70%, with CT-to-body divergence contributing to nondiagnostic sampling. This narrative review, prepared using the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles (SANRA), summarizes robotic-assisted bronchoscopy (RAB) platform technology, procedural optimization, diagnostic performance, safety, molecular tissue adequacy, and emerging applications. A structured search was updated through September 2026; this is not a systematic review. Using the strict definition recommended by the American Thoracic Society/American College of Chest Physicians (ATS/ACCP), the most comprehensive meta-analysis reported a pooled RAB diagnostic yield of 69.6%, while the prospective multicenter TARGET study reported an adjudicated strict yield of 61.6%. Higher pooled estimates of approximately 84-87% generally use intermediate definitions that the ATS/ACCP statement recommends against as primary diagnostic-yield measures. RAB pneumothorax rates are approximately 2% in pooled analyses, compared with approximately 20-25% for CT-guided transthoracic needle biopsy. In the randomized RELIANT trial, RAB was non-inferior, but not superior, to electromagnetic navigation bronchoscopy; in VERITAS, navigational bronchoscopy as a category was non-inferior to transthoracic needle biopsy for 12-month diagnostic accuracy, with fewer pneumothoraces. RAB is a useful option for selected PPLs, but strict-definition performance is more modest than frequently quoted intermediate yields. Outcomes depend on lesion characteristics, sampling strategy, operator experience, center volume, and imaging infrastructure.

title: Systemic, Pleural, and Alveolar Cytokine Responses After Video-Assisted Thoracoscopic Versus Open Lobectomy for Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: A Prospective Observational Study.
authors: Ancın B, Özercan MM, Yılmaz Y et al.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Surgical access and one-lung ventilation (OLV) may generate distinct systemic and local inflammatory responses after lung resection. We compared perioperative cytokine profiles in serum, pleural fluid, and bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) after video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) and open thoracotomy for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Methods: This prospective, single-center, non-randomized observational study included 40 adults undergoing anatomical lobectomy with mediastinal lymph-node dissection (VATS, n = 20; open thoracotomy, n = 20). Surgical access was selected according to patient preference. TNF-α, IL-6, IL-8, and IL-10 were measured in serial serum and pleural-fluid samples and in BAL from both lungs before OLV and after resection. Results: Serum and pleural-fluid cytokines peaked at 4 h in both groups. Exploratory pointwise comparisons showed that at 24 h, serum TNF-α (4.89 [IQR, 4.43-5.92] vs. 4.01 [IQR, 3.75-5.12] pg/mL; p = 0.010), IL-6 (150.22 [IQR, 136.90-194.66] vs. 108.00 [IQR, 100.46-125.88] pg/mL; p < 0.001), and IL-8 (66.83 [IQR, 57.70-82.82] vs. 43.62 [IQR, 32.89-50.59] pg/mL; p = 0.001) were higher after thoracotomy than after VATS; differences at 48 h persisted for TNF-α (2.48 [IQR, 1.86-3.04] vs. 1.99 [IQR, 1.19-2.23] pg/mL; p = 0.010) and IL-8 (16.92 [IQR, 15.09-23.99] vs. 7.42 [IQR, 6.44-11.30] pg/mL; p < 0.001). Pleural-fluid IL-6 at 24 h and IL-8 at 48 h were also higher after thoracotomy, whereas BAL cytokines did not differ significantly by approach. Longitudinal GEE analyses showed significant approach-by-time interactions for serum TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-8 and for pleural-fluid IL-8, but not for pleural-fluid IL-6. Conclusions: VATS was associated with a lower systemic proinflammatory response than open thoracotomy, while differences in the pleural compartment were more limited and no detectable difference was observed in early alveolar cytokine responses. These findings highlight compartment-specific differences in perioperative inflammatory responses between VATS and open thoracotomy.

title: Dose Mapping and Accumulation for Re-Irradiation of Lung Cancers: Methodological Principles, Uncertainties, Quality Assurance, and Practical Clinical Considerations.
authors: Rosu-Bubulac M, Zhong H, Chetty IJ
abstract: Background/Objectives: Thoracic re-irradiation is increasingly considered for recurrent, persistent, or new lung cancers after prior radiation therapy. The central clinical-technical challenge is relating prior and prospective doses across changes in anatomy, breathing state, fractionation, and imaging. Methods: This clinical-technical Perspective synthesizes consensus guidance, technical and the methodological literature, and representative clinical evidence to discuss rigid and deformable registration, dose mapping, biological normalization with EQD2/BED, uncertainty, quality assurance, and practical decision-making in lung re-irradiation. Results: Cumulative dose is an estimate with inherent uncertainty whose clinical value depends on the clinical question, anatomic stability, tissue correspondence, dose-transfer method, biological assumptions, and the consequence of error. Published cumulative dose constraints can provide useful orientation, but they are not universal pass/fail thresholds and should be interpreted together with their original endpoints, assumptions, and accumulation method. Conclusions: A focused, risk-adapted workflow can support more defensible use of cumulative dose in lung re-irradiation. Practical considerations in this article are intended to complement formal consensus guidance, institutional protocols, or patient-specific multidisciplinary judgment.

title: Successful First-Line Haploidentical Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation in an Elderly Patient With Severe Aplastic Anemia and Complex Comorbidities: A Case Report.
authors: Sun Y, Wang T, Wang X et al.
abstract: Standard management guidelines generally recommend immunosuppressive therapy (IST) as first-line treatment for older patients with severe aplastic anemia (SAA), whereas the role of upfront haploidentical hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (haplo-HSCT) in this population remains uncertain, particularly in patients with complex comorbidities. We report a 62-year-old woman with SAA, a history of surgically resected stage IA lung adenocarcinoma, and previous left lower extremity deep vein thrombosis treated with venous stent implantation and long-term aspirin therapy. Because no matched sibling or unrelated donor was available, and following individualized counseling regarding IST and transplantation, the patient underwent upfront haplo-HSCT combined with umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stem cells after a conditioning regimen including fludarabine, busulfan, cyclophosphamide, antithymocyte globulin, and thiotepa. Neutrophil engraftment occurred on post-transplant day +12, and platelet independence was achieved on day +13. Donor chimerism reached 99.6% by day +14 and remained within the complete-chimerism range through the latest available assessment in January 2026. In late December 2025 and January 2026, the patient developed cytomegalovirus infection accompanied by transient trilineage cytopenia; after anti-CMV treatment with maribavir, the infection was controlled and peripheral blood counts subsequently recovered. At the most recent clinical follow-up on August 6, 2026, approximately 17 months after transplantation, no chronic graft-versus-host disease had developed, the previous lung adenocarcinoma remained in remission, and the thrombotic condition remained clinically stable. This case suggests that upfront haplo-HSCT combined with UC-MSCs may represent a feasible individualized treatment option for carefully selected older patients with SAA who lack matched donors, although broader conclusions require larger studies and longer follow-up.

title: Ocular Immune Toxicity in Cancer Immunotherapy, From Immune Privilege Breakdown to Treatment Rechallenge: A Review.
authors: Chen KY, Chan HC, Lim M et al.
abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed cancer therapy but can disrupt ocular immune privilege and produce heterogeneous immune-related adverse events (Eye-irAEs). This structured narrative review with evidence mapping integrates clinical, epidemiologic, mechanistic, pharmacovigilance, and management data to define translational pathways from checkpoint blockade to ocular toxicity and treatment decisions. In a real-world cohort of 41,020 ICI-treated patients, ophthalmic irAEs occurred in 4.18% within 1 year, including dry eye disease in 2.00%, conjunctivitis in 0.87%, blepharitis in 0.51%, anterior uveitis in 0.39%, and keratitis in 0.38%. A 2026 meta-analysis of five cohorts comprising 277,790 participants found increased uveitis risk with ICI exposure (hazard ratio 2.26), while pooled overall survival was not significantly associated with ICI-related uveitis (hazard ratio 0.69, 95% CI 0.35-1.39). Among patients with preexisting uveitis, recurrence reached 38.9% for prior anterior disease and 51.1% for prior intermediate, posterior, or panuveitis. Risk varies by malignancy and regimen; melanoma was associated with substantially greater noninfectious uveitis than lung cancer (1.10% vs 0.18%; risk ratio 6.17, 95% CI 4.20-9.08). Mechanistically, PD-1/PD-L1 and CTLA-4 have the strongest established exposure-toxicity evidence, LAG-3 signals are emerging, and TIM-3 and TIGIT remain translational. Phenotype-directed local or systemic therapy can preserve vision and permit ICI continuation or rechallenge in selected patients. In a 2026 rechallenge series, four of five rechallenged patients had no documented recurrence, while one recurrence resolved successfully with corticosteroid treatment. Standardized phenotyping, longitudinal ophthalmic surveillance, multidisciplinary attribution, and prospective ocular endpoints should translate mechanistic insight into safer immunotherapy, individualized rechallenge, and improved cancer-treatment continuity.

title: Preliminary results of the STARLORD study: a mono-institutional prospective phase II experience of STereotActic Radiotherapy for LOcally advanced non small cell lung cancer ineligible for concurrent chemoRaDiation.
authors: Cuccia F, Campione M, Mortellaro G et al.
abstract:
AIMS: For patients with unresectable stage III non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) ineligible for concurrent chemo-radiation (cCRT), stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) may provide a favorable efficacy-toxicity balance.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: STARLORD (STereotActic Radiotherapy for LOcally advanced non--small cell lung cancer ineligible for concurrent chemoRaDiation) is a prospective phase II study evaluating safety and early outcomes of SBRT after chemotherapy is delivered with Radixact system.
RESULTS: Twenty-six consecutive patients with stage IIIB-IIIC NSCLC were analyzed with median age 75.5 years (IQR, 72.2-79.8), with 84.6% of patients presenting stage IIIB disease and 15.4% stage IIIC. Following induction chemotherapy, SBRT was delivered to both the primary tumor and mediastinal disease in 5 fractions, for median total doses, respectively, of 40 Gy (IQR, 40-45 Gy) and 35 Gy (IQR, 35-40 Gy). Consolidation immunotherapy was administered in 76.9% of patients. After a median follow-up of 17.3 months, acute grade 3 (G3) dysphagia was observed in 7.7%, no late grade ≥3 toxicities were observed. The 1-year local control (LC) rate was 86.7%, with two mediastinal progressions occurring 11 and 12 months after SBRT. Median distant progression-free survival (mDPFS) was 15.6 months with a 1-year DPFS rate of 56.7%. Four deaths were recorded during follow-up, resulting in a 1-year overall survival (OS) rate of 90.9%, with worse outcomes for patients with stage IIIC disease (log-rank P = .00027) and aged ≥75 years (log-rank P = .032).
CONCLUSIONS: In our experience, for frailer patients with unresectable locally advanced NSCLC, SBRT is well tolerated and provides promising disease control outcomes.

title: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-related myocarditis, myositis, and myasthenia gravis overlap syndrome: a single-center case series and systematic review.
authors: Soriano J, Martínez-Rubiño M, Vicente Elcano M et al.
abstract:
PURPOSE: The aim of our study was to evaluate the clinical, diagnostic, therapeutic, and prognostic features of immune checkpoint inhibitor-related myocarditis, myositis, and myasthenia gravis overlap syndrome (IM3OS).
METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective case series of seven patients with IM3OS treated at Hospital del Mar between 2020 and 2025, together with a systematic review and descriptive patient-level synthesis of the published literature. PubMed/MEDLINE and Embase were searched for reports published between 2015 and 2025, following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Eligible studies included case reports, case series, letters, correspondence, and conference abstracts providing sufficient individual patient-level data.
RESULTS: In our series, all seven patients were male, with a median age of 81 years. The most frequent tumor types were non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) (42.8%) and urothelial carcinoma (28.5%). Diplopia (71.4%), ptosis (71.4%), and dyspnea (71.4%) were the most common presenting manifestations. Most patients received high-dose corticosteroids (71.4%), intravenous immunoglobulins (85.7%), and additional non-steroidal immunosuppressive agents (85.7%). The systematic review included 71 studies and 103 patients. Median age was 71 years, and 68.9% were male. Melanoma (35.9%), renal cell carcinoma (16.5%), and NSCLC (16.5%) were the most frequent malignancies. Ptosis (71.8%) and weakness (62.1%) were the most common presenting symptoms. The most frequently reported initial regimen was methylprednisolone 1 g/day (35.9%), and 52.4% of patients received additional non-steroidal immunosuppressive agents.
CONCLUSION: IM3OS is a rare, early-onset, clinically severe immune-related overlap syndrome with a high mortality rate requiring prompt recognition, structured multisystem assessment, close cardiorespiratory monitoring, and multidisciplinary management. Current evidence remains observational and does not allow conclusions regarding therapeutic superiority.
